Provides columns for actual values,forecast,OB, previous year values, and variances.
Provide a complete variance?bridge decomposition (Vol, Mix, Price, Cost, Other, Real Var) to explain why CY differs from PY,RF,OB at any P&L line.
Expose detailed cost sub?components split into CY, PY,RF,OB and Var — supporting deeper diagnostic and root?cause analysis.

MC is marginal contribution, GP is gross profit, PC is product contribution
business_facts:
Enables end?to?end financial analysis covering revenue, margins, costs, and profitability for PMI by brand family and brand differentiator.
Supports multi?year and multi?version (Actuals - AC, Rolling Forecasts - RF, Original Budgeted - OB etc.) comparisons at any account line
Allows analysts to compare performance to Previous year performance (AC vs AC),Annual plan targets (AC vs OB), Latest and updated rolling forecats (AC vs RF).OB is the company’s initial operating plan established at the start of the year. 

OB remains unchanged throughout the year.Used for measuring target achievement and whether the company met its original commitments.
Rolling Forecasts are revised every quarter using the latest sales trends, market signals, and updated assumptions. RF3 means rolling forecasts as per March.
RF11 is the last rolling foreacst of the year updated in November, usually more accurate than the beginning?of?year budget.
There is no December update to RF as OB is updated in December
Use OB when evaluating performance vs annual plan or target.Use RF when evaluating performance vs latest expected outcome or most realistic forecast.
Sheet also provides decomposition into: Volume, Mix, Price, Cost, FX, Other, Real Variation.
Real Variation is computed as:
Real = Volume + Mix + Price + ex?Manufacturing + CC409 + SVC + FME + Other (Excludes currency fluctuation impact FX)
Total variance can be expressed as:FX + Real
These act as drivers which can be used to explain the drivers of performance variance between CY and PY or vs forecast/budget.
Any expression written as '<Year1> AC vs <Year2> AC' means a comparison where Year1 is the current year (CY) and Year2 is the previous year (PY). Example: ' AC 2025 vs AC 2024' means 2025= CY and 2024= PY.

It  enables consistent comparison between Marlboro offerings and relevant products from other major tobacco manufacturers. This file can be used to support downstream analytics such as SKU clustering, competitive benchmarking, pricing architecture evaluation, pack?level substitution analysis
Link with INDIA_SEGMENTATION to analyse trends and movement in market shares and sales of PMI's SKUs vs competitive SKUs (TMOs); help to map Marlboro variants to corresponding competitor SKUs in the market, understand competitive intensity within each price, length, and format segment
Also link with NIELSEN_VARIANT to analyse the value and volume market share changes in PMI's SKUs and competitive SKUs

It also enables integration with broader market datasets to understand how Marlboro’s performance compares to competitor SKUs at both value and volume levels across markets.

This file should also be used to understand which variants (column F) fall under which length and price segment (Column A and B respectively). This would help in doing the mix movement analysis. 
Uptrading is indicated when volume growth shifts toward Premium (King Size) and High Price segments, with slower growth or decline in Value (Pocket Filter)—showing consumers moving to higher-priced products.
Downtrading is the opposite: rising volumes in Value and possibly High, while Premium declines or underperforms, signaling price sensitivity.
If Premium grows faster than total market, mix is improving (premiumization); if Value outgrows, mix is diluting.
Stable total volume with segment mix shifting upward still indicates uptrading, even without overall growth.
You should compare relative growth rates across segments, not just absolute volumes, to infer mix movement.

business_facts:
This contains month?on?month financial shipment volumes for each cigarette variant, enabling analysis of how individual variants contribute to overall company performance.
This data is the volume sold by PMI to its primary distributor GPI.
It supports identification of sales fluctuations, growth patterns, and performance declines, helping detect emerging demand trends, seasonality effects, or volume disruptions. It contributes to demand forecasting and portfolio planning by showing how shipment volumes evolve over time and which variants are gaining or losing momentum. Increases or decreases in shipment volumes generally translate into secondary?market volume shifts with a lag of 1–2 months.

This file is also used to calculate Bias (%) and Sales Forecast Accuracy (SFA) based on two lag periods:
M-1 (Lag of 1 period)
M-3 (Lag of 3 periods)

Definition of Lags
M-1 (Lag 1):
Compares the actual sales of a given month with the forecast for that same month prepared in the previous month.
M-3 (Lag 3):
Compares the actual sales of a given month with the forecast for that same month prepared three months earlier.

Data Selection Rules
Actual Values:
Always take actuals from the folder corresponding to the current month under analysis.
Forecast Values:
For M-1: Take the forecast for the current month from the previous month’s folder.
For M-3: Take the forecast for the current month from the folder three months prior (e.g., for April actuals, use the forecast from January).
Ensure the forecast corresponds to the same variant/segment.

Formulas
Bias (%)
M-1 Bias:
Bias %=(Actual?Forecast (M-1))/Forecast (M-1)×100
M-3 Bias:
Bias %=(Actual?Forecast (M-3))/Forecast (M-3)×100
Sales Forecast Accuracy (SFA)
SFA=1??Bias %
(Use absolute bias to reflect accuracy regardless of under- or over-forecasting.)

Summary Example
For December analysis:
Actuals: From December folder
M-1 Forecast: From November folder
M-3 Forecast: From September folder

business_facts:
Sales Forecasting Accuracy (SFA) - Measures how close forecasted sales are to actual financial shipments for a given month. High SFA indicates effective demand planning and alignment across operations and sales teams. Low accuracy may signal forecasting errors or demand volatility. Definition of M-1 (Lag 1): Compares the actual sales of a given month with the forecast for that same month prepared in the previous month. Definition of M-3 (Lag 3): Compares the actual sales of a given month with the forecast for that same month prepared three months earlier.

Bias - Indicates systematic over- or under-forecasting in sales predictions. Positive bias means consistent overestimation, while negative bias reflects underestimation. Helps identify structural issues in forecasting rather than random error. Definition of M-1 (Lag 1): Compares the actual sales of a given month with the forecast for that same month prepared in the previous month. Definition of M-3 (Lag 3): Compares the actual sales of a given month with the forecast for that same month prepared three months earlier.

Customer Fill Rate - Represents the percentage of customer demand fulfilled from available inventory without stockouts. A high fill rate shows strong service levels and supply reliability. Low fill rate may lead to lost sales and reduced customer satisfaction.

Productivity 

LOGD - Quantifies loss of goods and is the write-off done in a particular month, value is cumulative from January to December and resets to 0 in January of new year. 

Ageing Inventory @WH (> 9 months) - Measures the proportion or value of inventory that has been in stock for more than 9 months. High ageing inventory signals slow-moving stock, risk of obsolescence, and working capital inefficiencies.

Innovation Index - Captures the contribution of new products volume (launched in last 24 months) to total volume sales. A higher index reflects stronger innovation adoption and portfolio renewal.

KS SOS - Measures the market share of King Size variant in PMI portfolio compared to competitors.

Brand Equity (PMI & Competition, Brand Perception + Brand Loyalty) - Assesses overall brand strength including awareness and trails versus competitors.

MI Activities - Tracks execution and frequency of competitive intelligence and market insights gathering activities. Includes monitoring competitor pricing, promotions, and consumer trends to inform strategy.

IPM DSD - No of Outlets ('000) - Represents the number of outlets served through Direct Store Delivery (DSD) by PMI distributor GPI. Indicates the reach and direct distribution footprint in the market.

IPM Availability - No of Outlets ('000) - Measures how many outlets have PMI products available for sale at a given time. Reflects product penetration and distribution effectiveness.

Visibility Expansion Ach - Tracks the achievement of in-store visibility targets such as displays, signage, and merchandising units. Higher achievement indicates better brand presence and influence at the point of sale.

business_facts: Market visit survey data provides qualitative intelligence from the field to complement quantitative sales and volume data. It captures real-time ground signals such as shifts in consumer purchase behavior (e.g., from KS to RF due to price increases), fastest-moving products observed at outlets, new product traction, and presence of illicit/imported brands. This data is particularly useful for early detection of demand shifts before they appear in secondary volume or financial shipment data. It helps identify risk areas (e.g., downtrading, illicit brand growth) and opportunities (e.g., NPL traction, RF segment growth) at a city or market level. Can be used alongside SECONDARY_VOLUME and FINANCIAL_SHIPMENT data to correlate field observations with actual volume movements. Useful for understanding trade margin impacts, branding effectiveness, and distributor/retailer sentiment.
